column1: # tests/docker/rehearsal-cells.tsv — the WS4 rehearsal cells and the topology each one pins.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (H8). A rehearsal cell has two version axes and only one of them was ever
# written down. The arm — which wp-slimstat a site is upgrading FROM — is pinned in arms.sha256.
# The topology — which WordPress and which PHP that site is running WHILE it upgrades — was a
# default in rehearse-upgrade.sh (WP 6.7 / PHP 8.2) that every cell silently inherited, and a
# default is not a pin: it moves when the default moves, and a recorded PASS then describes a
# topology nobody can reconstruct.
# It matters more than a bookkeeping fix, because the obvious pairing is the WRONG one. The
# tempting reading of "rehearse the 4.8.1 upgrade" is 2019 plugin on 2019 WordPress on 2019 PHP.
# That is not what the 12.9 % of installs still on 4.8.x are. A site stuck on a 2019 plugin is
# overwhelmingly a site whose WordPress core kept auto-updating and whose host kept moving PHP
# forward underneath it — the plugin is old precisely BECAUSE nobody has touched it, and core
# updates itself while plugins do not. So the cell that matters is 4.8.1 on a MODERN WordPress.
# PHP is the other half, and it is pinned DOWN rather than up for the vintages: 4.8.1 predates
# PHP 8 by two years, and the question a 4.8.1 cell has to answer first is whether that code
# even loads before the upgrade can start. 7.4 is the oldest PHP this programme supports and the
# newest one 4.8.1 was written against, which makes it the version where a fatal is a finding
# about the upgrade rather than a foregone conclusion.
# If the 4.8.1 arm fatals on WP 6.7 before the upgrade path is reached, THAT IS THE FINDING and
# the cell records it as such. It is not a reason to soften the topology until the cell goes
# green: a site that cannot load the old plugin on current WordPress cannot take the upgrade
# either, and knowing that is worth more than a green cell that pretended otherwise.
# HOW IT IS USED. run-topologies.sh and rehearse-upgrade.sh read the row for their cell and
# export TOPOLOGY_WP / TOPOLOGY_PHP from it; the values land in the cell's verdict, so a recorded
# result names the topology it was produced on. Environment still wins for a one-off, which is
# how a "does it also fail on 8.2?" question gets asked without editing this file.
# tests/rehearsal-vintage-corpus-test.php asserts every cell here declares both pins and that
# each arm version appears in arms.sha256 — an undeclared pin is the default coming back.
